pr_title: roachprod,roachtest: use roachprod stage for older cockroach binaries
pr_body:
Previously, the version upgrade roachtests used binfetcher to fetch
older cockroach binaries, which doesn't work as-is with the geos
libraries that are now included with our releases. This was blocking
mixed version 20.2/21.1 testing.

This PR replaces all the uses of binfetcher with `roachprod stage` to
download older cockroach releases in roachtests. It also adds an
optional`--dir` flag to `roachprod stage` to specify the directory to
stage the binary and libraries to, which is needed for the mixed-version
tests because they need to keep the old binaries and libraries around in
order to downgrade.

Closes #55706.

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/56163)

This could use some cleanup, and there's a TODO about supporting the `--dir` flag for `stage cockroach` and `stage workload`, but I wanted to get some feedback first. This is a prerequisite for #55520 and adding a `v21.1.0-alpha.00000000` tag on master.

As of this PR, there are two remaining uses of binfetcher:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6ad82700963338c3854821d2e98b0612d0f04af6/pkg/cmd/roachtest/scaledata.go#L77-L86

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/61dbe00c0ef74df68fad46530f32bd6e9f8b3c20/pkg/cmd/roachtest/tpchvec.go#L593-L603

Can both be converted to use `roachprod stage` instead? Then we can delete the binfetcher package, which seems like the easier option - the alternative is fixing it.
I'm on board with these proposed improvements, but how would you feel about merging this now and opening some issues for later? I'm eager to unblock, e.g., #56190.

Sounds good!

issue_context.title: util: binfetcher can't handle lib directory
issue_context.body:
`binfetcher` currently can't handle the `lib` directory included in our most recent release tarballs and will return an error `archive contains more than one file`.

This is currently blocking us from being able to run any of the mixed-version roachtests (which need to download a binary for the previous release), which itself is blocking us from being able to add a v21.1.0 tag, etc.
comments: @kenliu and @jlinder, this is an urgent problem. Not having mixed-version roachtests is a serious, blocking issue for the whole organization. Would you be able to get this done this week?

To be clear, when I said "any of the mixed-version roachtests" I meant for 20.2/21.1. All our release branches will be fine, and `master` is fine for now. But since `master` still counts as "20.2," we're likely going to start having problems with our existing mixed-version tests once we start introducing changes in 21.1 that are not compatible with 20.1.
Thanks, Lucy. I think this problem is still severe, and needs attention - if we drop it now, it'll come back soon enough. Ken and James, do you have room to take this on?
@jordanlewis If this is an urgent problem that blocks an upcoming release then we will give it a high priority to fix. Who else has the knowledge to assist with this if needed?
Great! Lucy has recent context on the problem. Binfetcher is a very short program that was written by Tobi in 2017 judging from git blame.
It lives in `pkg/util/binfetcher/binfetcher.go` in the CockroachDB repo.

I thought about this a bit more, and I don't think it's a good idea to have binfetcher handle this by just indiscriminately copying the `lib` directory wherever we put the cockroach binary (like I was originally thinking), since for mixed-version tests we might clobber the libraries for whatever current version we staged, among other potential issues.

@otan I figure you might have thoughts about how to handle this. What's the best way to download an earlier version of cockroach with the libraries so we can use it in the mixed-version tests? Could we just use `roachprod stage` (and make sure we preserve the contents of `lib` for each version)? Maybe I should ask that last question to a wider audience.
@otan and I discussed offline. It seems like we should be able to just use `roachprod stage release` into a separate directory to preserve each version's `lib` directory.

review_comments: Doesn't this download the same binary in a loop? Can `c.Stage` or even `roachprod stage` do the caching so we don't have to be smart about each invocation of `c.Stage`?
